_directive: R1 QUESTIONER output for the machines (knit_machine_strategist) self-improvement loop, segment T12, round 1. These are the hardest questions this specialist CLAIMS (via competency_questions_covered, owns[], decision_procedure, conflicts_and_dominance) to be able to answer but is most likely to answer weakly, staleley, inconsistently, or by over-claiming. Written by an adversary who wants the specialist to fail. NOT answered here (R2 answers, R3 judges). Honesty binding preserved: gaps are FINDINGS not inventions; the three governing blockers stay [UNKNOWN]; off-paper stays mechanism; cotton duty ~16.5% never ~7%.

questions.q: You call building our own knitting machine the 'single highest-confidence NEVER' at ~$2M-10M+ over 3-7 years vs a sub-$20k used machine. That $2M-10M+ figure is tagged [ESTIMATE, HIGH on direction]. Give the method, basis and component build-up behind $2M-10M+ (what does the number decompose into, and against what comparable), and state precisely what is [ESTIMATE] vs what is genuinely [FACT] inside that verdict. If the dollar magnitude has no derivation and rests only on the Groz-Beckert-makes-the-needles / software-only-open-research facts, say so.
questions.targets: the build-NEVER verdict and its cost basis (owns[]: 'the build-NEVER verdict and the periphery-only reverse-engineering rule'; competency: 'Why is building our own knitting machine the single highest-confidence NEVER, and on what cost basis?')
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claim / fake-precision hiding as an [ESTIMATE]: a wide $2M-10M+ band presented as if load-bearing when the number may be an unanchored guess; the correct verdict (NEVER) may be right for reasons that do NOT include a defensible dollar figure, so the specialist could be smuggling a fabricated-precision cost into a labeled-estimate wrapper.
questions.why_load_bearing: the build-NEVER call is the specialist's marquee dominance rule and an N4 anti-hype anchor for the whole brain; if its cost basis is invented rather than derived, the flagship verdict rests on a number the specialist cannot defend.

questions.q: The HSN-8447 landed stack is stated as '~7.5% BCD (+~0.75% surcharge) + 18% IGST'. This is a MACHINE import into India under heading 8447. Confirm you are NOT conflating this with the GARMENT import duty into the US under heading 6110 (cotton ~16.5% / wool ~16% / acrylic-MMF ~32%). State which of the 8447 numbers is [FACT] vs [ESTIMATE] vs [UNKNOWN] per your own boundary, and confirm no residual ~7% cotton-duty figure or any 6110 rate has leaked into your machine-import math.
questions.targets: the HSN-8447 landed import stack (owns[]: 'consolidate honest per-class cost bands and the HSN-8447 landed import stack'; competency: 'What import cost does a knitting machine carry into India under HSN 8447?')
questions.failure_mode_probed: stale/cross-contamination: the discredited ~7% cotton figure or a 6110 garment rate bleeding into the 8447 machine-import stack, or the ~7.5% BCD being asserted as [FACT] when the spec itself tags the BCD sub-heading [ESTIMATE] and 2025-26 changes [UNKNOWN] — an internal inconsistency between the number quoted and its own honesty tag.
questions.why_load_bearing: duty discipline (N5) is a hard brain-wide gate; a machine specialist that muddles 8447-vs-6110 or lets ~7% survive violates the corrected duty trio and the estimate-vs-fact split it explicitly claims to enforce.

questions.q: Your throughput bands are: computerised flat ~12-25 garments'-worth of panels/machine/shift, a linker ~20-45 sweaters/linker/shift, whole-garment ~6-15/machine/shift. If a knitting machine does 12-25 and a linker does 20-45, on those numbers a single linker can KEEP UP WITH or OUTPACE a single knitting machine — which contradicts your headline claim that 'the linker, not the knitting machine, caps daily output.' Reconcile this precisely: at what machine:linker ratio does linking actually become the ceiling, and does your own band data support 'linker is THE bottleneck' or only 'linking is A constraint at scale'?
questions.targets: line capacity sized off the linker bottleneck (owns[]: 'line capacity sized off the linker + programmer bottleneck'; competency: 'Why is the linker, not the knitting machine, the step that caps how many sweaters a small line ships per day, and how do the throughput bands prove it?')
questions.failure_mode_probed: internal contradiction / over-claim: the specialist's own [ESTIMATE] throughput bands may numerically undercut its central 'linker is the bottleneck' thesis; it claims the bands PROVE the bottleneck but on their face they may show the opposite for a 1:1 line, meaning the load-bearing claim is asserted, not demonstrated.
questions.why_load_bearing: the linker-and-programmer-dominates-the-iron rule is the specialist's #1 conflict-resolution and sizing principle; if the numbers it cites as proof actually contradict it, every capacity plan and every buy-sizing verdict downstream inherits the flaw.

questions.q: Write out the breakeven_utilisation formula you own and actually plug numbers into it to produce the buy-used trigger for THIS brand. You state breakeven = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity). But jobwork_unit_rate is the Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate, which is a GOVERNING [UNKNOWN] blocker. Show the arithmetic, and if the formula cannot be evaluated because its key input is [UNKNOWN], state plainly that your entire buy-vs-subcontract breakeven is undecidable until that rate is measured — do not invent a rate to make it compute.
questions.targets: the utilisation breakeven gated on the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate (owns[]: 'the subcontract->buy-used->never-build acquisition ladder and the utilisation breakeven'; competency: 'How is the buy-vs-subcontract breakeven computed on utilisation, and what utilisation flips the decision?')
questions.failure_mode_probed: fabrication-to-fill-a-gap OR undue-certainty: the temptation to invent a jobwork_unit_rate so the formula yields a tidy breakeven, versus the honest answer that the breakeven is structurally undecidable because it depends on the knit+LINK [UNKNOWN] (G2). Either the specialist fabricates, or it must concede its own owned breakeven cannot be computed.
questions.why_load_bearing: the breakeven is the hinge that decides Phase-0-subcontract vs Phase-1-buy-used; the honesty binding says the knit+LINK rate stays [UNKNOWN] and is 'decided around, never invented' — this question forces the specialist to either honor or violate that on its own central formula.

questions.q: You hold 'AI-design->knit-program autonomy on our acrylic/blend fabrics' at [UNKNOWN] and delegate it to T8/design. Yet you also name 'design->knit-program assist' as the SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE AI use because it offsets the scarce programmer. Draw the exact line: what specifically can AI do TODAY on the CAD/flat-knit programmer bottleneck (Shima APEX / Stoll M1plus) that you will endorse as a [FACT]-or-defensible-[ESTIMATE] multiplier, versus what crosses into the [UNKNOWN] autonomy you refuse to assume? If pressed, does 'highest-value AI use' collapse into 'a use whose actual payoff is [UNKNOWN]'?
questions.targets: AI-as-multiplier-not-substitute on the machine layer (owns[]: 'AI-as-multiplier-not-substitute on the machine layer'; competency: 'What is the single highest-value AI use here... and which AI claims are hype?')
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claim by relabeling: promoting AI design->program assist to 'highest-value' while its real autonomy is [UNKNOWN] risks selling a hoped-for capability as a present multiplier — the exact AI-hype failure mode N4 guards against; the specialist may be unable to name any concrete, present-tense, defensible AI action that is NOT actually the [UNKNOWN] autonomy in disguise.
questions.why_load_bearing: AI-multiplier-not-substitute is a cross-specialist dominance rule and a standing brain failure mode; if the specialist's own 'highest-value use' is really the [UNKNOWN] autonomy dressed up, it is over-promising on AI at the machine layer.

questions.q: The CAD/flat-knit programmer bottleneck is vendor-locked: 'a Shima program is not a Stoll program.' After the 2025 Stoll flat-knit exit you say new-build narrows to Shima + Chinese and the used pool deepens. If the brand buys a used ex-Stoll machine (cheap, deep pool) it inherits the Stoll M1plus/knitelligence toolchain and Obertshausen-only service; if it standardises on Shima APEX it pays more but gets the surviving ecosystem. Which does your verdict actually pick for a micro brand, and does buying into a DISCONTINUED vendor's locked toolchain — for the very bottleneck skill (programmer) you call the strategy's hinge — contradict your own buy-used-Chinese-first default?
questions.targets: the acquisition ladder + programmer bottleneck + Stoll-exit market read (owns[]: 'machine-family selection', 'the subcontract->buy-used->never-build acquisition ladder'; competency on the Stoll exit reshaping the choice)
questions.failure_mode_probed: unresolved internal tension / evasion: the specialist may wave at 'buy-used' and 'Chinese-first' and 'Stoll pool deepens' without confronting that a used Stoll buy locks the brand's scarcest resource (the programmer) into a dead, service-constrained toolchain — a real strategic conflict it may paper over rather than resolve.
questions.why_load_bearing: the programmer bottleneck is called the hinge of the whole strategy; if the acquisition ladder's cheapest path (used Stoll) undermines the hinge, the verdict is incoherent unless the specialist explicitly steers to Shima-or-Chinese and accepts the cost.

questions.q: The periphery-only reverse-engineering rule permits 'jigs, fixtures, non-critical spares, cam-timing learning, scanning worn obsolete brackets' but forbids the core kinematic chain and firmware/knit-CAD cloning. Give the EXACT test that separates 'periphery' from 'core' for a concrete borderline case: is a worn needle-bed alignment gauge periphery? A replacement cam follower? A 3D-printed carrier bracket that touches yarn path? If the line is 'anything not the needle bed / needles / cams / selection / firmware / CAD,' show that it actually decides these cases rather than restating the two lists.
questions.targets: the periphery-only reverse-engineering rule (owns[]: 'the build-NEVER verdict and the periphery-only reverse-engineering rule'; competency: 'where may reverse-engineering and 3D-printing genuinely help?')
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / non-operational rule: the periphery-vs-core boundary may be a slogan (two lists) with no decision test for the ambiguous parts that actually matter (anything mechanically adjacent to but not inside the core chain), so the rule cannot adjudicate the cases a builder would really face — a hole in an owned deliverable.
questions.why_load_bearing: reverse-engineering is where the build-NEVER discipline is most likely to erode in practice ('it's just a spare'); if the boundary is not operational, the specialist cannot actually hold the line it claims to own, and IP/legal exposure creeps in.

questions.q: Your per-class price bands include a used Chinese Cixing-class machine at ~$4,000-15,000 [ESTIMATE, MED] and a used hand-flat at ~$200-1,500. You explicitly downgrade tidy anchors like '~$15k used Chinese machine' to wide LOW-MED bands 'needing a landed quote.' But you also compute a landed stack on top (freight + BCD + IGST + install). For the Cixing-class case, what is the LANDED number after the 8447 stack, and given you have NO landed vendor quote and the BCD sub-heading is [ESTIMATE] and 2025-26 changes [UNKNOWN], is any landed figure you produce defensible — or is 'sub-$20k used' (the anchor of the build-NEVER comparison) itself an ungrounded band stacked on an ungrounded band?
questions.targets: per-class cost bands + landed stack + the sub-$20k anchor of build-NEVER (owns[]: 'consolidate honest per-class cost bands and the HSN-8447 landed import stack')
questions.failure_mode_probed: compounding-uncertainty / hidden fake-precision: the 'sub-$20k used' figure that anchors the build-NEVER contrast is a wide FOB band with an [ESTIMATE] duty stack and [UNKNOWN] budget changes on top; the specialist may quote a clean landed number that its own honesty rules forbid, or must admit the build-NEVER comparison rests on a band-on-a-band with no landed quote.
questions.why_load_bearing: the whole build-NEVER economics ($2M-10M+ vs sub-$20k) depends on the sub-$20k side being real; if that side is as ungrounded as the build side, the comparison's rhetorical force outruns its evidence.

questions.q: The Ludhiana job-work mesh is your Phase-0 default: 'subcontract knit+link+finish into the agglomeration.' The brain describes an off-paper economy (cash job-work, informal/contract labour, patchy enforcement) as a structural MECHANISM with magnitudes [UNKNOWN]. When you recommend subcontracting knit+link into that mesh at capsule scale, how do you surface that the job-work piece rate you depend on is entangled with the off-paper mechanism — WITHOUT (a) turning it into a named-party accusation, (b) inventing a magnitude, or (c) ignoring it entirely? Show the honest framing, or concede this is out of your lane and route it to Ludhiana while still flagging the dependency.
questions.targets: the subcontract-into-the-mesh default + the off-paper dependency (owns[]: 'the subcontract->buy-used->never-build acquisition ladder'; decision_procedure Phase-0 default; boundary: routes cost magnitudes and legal exposure to confirmation)
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope/honesty double-bind: the specialist may either (i) ignore that its Phase-0 job-work default sits on the off-paper mechanism, (ii) drift into accusation, or (iii) invent a rate — all violations. The correct move (name the mechanism structurally, hold magnitude [UNKNOWN], defer the number to Ludhiana/mfg_economics) is subtle and easy to fumble.
questions.why_load_bearing: N3 (off-paper as mechanism, never accusation, magnitude [UNKNOWN]) is a hard brain gate, and the specialist's entire launch posture depends on the job-work mesh; mishandling the off-paper entanglement is a direct honesty-gate failure on the specialist's most-used recommendation.

questions.q: Your validation_checklist demands capacity be 'sized off the linker-and-programmer ceiling' and every buy stated as a 'buy-machine-plus-linkers-plus-programmer decision.' Take a concrete target — say 50 finished sweaters/day of A2 12GG fully-fashioned — and produce the actual capacity plan: how many knitting machines, how many linkers, how many programmers, at what utilisation, and what does it cost to staff/acquire. If you cannot produce integer counts because the throughput bands are [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] and the linker labour rate and programmer availability/rate are [UNKNOWN], state that your owned 'capacity plan' output is a structure-only sketch, not a sizing — and name every input that blocks a real number.
questions.targets: the capacity plan sized off the bottleneck (owns[]: 'line capacity sized off the linker + programmer bottleneck'; capability output: 'a capacity plan sized off the linker-and-programmer ceiling with the matching linker/programmer count named'; competency Q14 merged verdict + capacity plan)
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap between promised deliverable and deliverable-able output: the spec claims a 'capacity plan' with 'matching linker/programmer count named,' but every quantitative input (throughput bands LOW-MED, linker rate [UNKNOWN], programmer availability [UNKNOWN]) is too soft to yield integer counts; the specialist may over-claim a real plan it cannot actually produce, or must downgrade it to a structure-only sketch.
questions.why_load_bearing: 'sized off the bottleneck' is the specialist's signature capability and appears in its validation checklist; if it cannot instantiate a single concrete capacity plan without fabricating rates, the capability is aspirational and the checklist item is unmeetable as written.

questions.q: The 2025 Stoll/KARL MAYER flat-knit exit (Reutlingen closed 31 Oct 2025, China production ended Dec 2025, service via Obertshausen only) is tagged [FACT] and is load-bearing for 'new narrows to Shima + Chinese, used pool deepens.' Today is 2026-07-01. Give the citation/basis for each dated claim, state your knowledge-cutoff exposure, and identify what in this market-structure read is now potentially STALE (e.g., has the used-pool-deepening actually materialised, are Obertshausen parts still flowing, did any successor pick up Stoll service). If you cannot verify post-exit reality, mark the downstream 'used pool deepens / buy-used reinforced' inference as [ESTIMATE] leaning on a [FACT] that is itself now a year old.
questions.targets: the Stoll-exit market-structure read (owns[]: 'a market-structure read with the ex-Stoll diligence item'; competency: 'How does the 2025 Stoll flat-knit exit reshape the new-build choice and the used pool?'; escalation trigger on ex-Stoll parts-and-service)
questions.failure_mode_probed: stale [FACT] / unverified inference: dated 2025 events asserted as durable [FACT] that drive a 2026 buy-used verdict, without acknowledging the reasoning ('used pool deepens,' 'reinforces buy-used') is a downstream [ESTIMATE] that may not have materialised and depends on facts now a year past cutoff — an over-reliance on a freshness-decayed anchor.
questions.why_load_bearing: the Stoll exit is the specialist's freshest [FACT] and the pillar of its new-vs-used and diligence read; if it treats a year-old dated event and its speculative market consequences as fixed truth, the acquisition verdict rests on a possibly-stale foundation the loop is meant to catch.
